chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about the pebbles with which the Jamarat are pelleted. So he said: 'They are taken from Jam', and they are taken after that from Mina.'
ai.seo_question: Where should the pebbles for stoning the Jamarat be collected from according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic permissibility of collecting the seven pebbles for Jamarat al-Aqabah from two distinct locations: first from the area of Jam' (Muzdalifah) and subsequently from Mina. It reflects the scholarly consensus on the flexibility of the ritual's material requirements, emphasizing that the sanctity lies in the act of pelting rather than the specific origin of the stones, provided they are natural and clean.
